title: SDK + API primitives for traffic-split rollouts, shadowing, and safe auto-rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add first-class API endpoints and SDK helpers to orchestrate model rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) and to support safe auto-rollback. The goal is to give platform and product teams a consistent, auditable, and idempotent surface for: creating a rollout, adjusting traffic splits, promoting or aborting canaries, running shadow experiments without affecting responses, and specifying automatic rollback policies based on SLA/quality signals. This ticket scopes the API surface, SDK ergonomics, permissions model, idempotency semantics, and acceptance criteria. Implementation will be coordinated with ENG tickets that implement runtime routing + metrics hooks.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/rollouts creates a rollout resource (canary, AB, or shadow) and returns a stable rollout_id
API: PATCH /v1/rollouts/{id}/traffic updates traffic split with optimistic concurrency and idempotency token support
SDK: client.rollouts.create_canary(...) helper exists that accepts model_id, baseline_id, traffic_percentage, metrics_watchlist, and rollback_policy
SDK: helper methods are idempotent using an optional client-provided idempotency_key; server dedup behavior documented
Permissions: RBAC roles enforced (rollout_admin, rollout_operator, rollout_viewer) and mapping documented
Observability: rollout events emitted to audit log with actor, timestamp, delta, and reason; Console shows live traffic split and health metrics
Auto-rollback: server-side policy triggers rollback when configured signal thresholds breach and emits an explicit rollback event
Shadow traffic: endpoint accepts a shadow=true flag; shadowed requests are delivered to target model without counting quotas or altering production response path
Docs & SDK samples: user guide, API contract, and TypeScript + Python examples published
End-to-end test: QA harness can create a canary, shift traffic, simulate metric regressions, and observe auto-rollback within configured window
design_decisions: Rollout as first-class resource: persist rollout metadata so operations are addressable and auditable
Traffic updates via PATCH with if-match ETag header for optimistic concurrency to avoid races from multiple operators
Optional idempotency_key on mutating endpoints: server stores a short-lived mapping to returned rollout mutation result
Shadow traffic uses same routing path but a 'shadow' tag and never modifies customer-facing response; shadow mode can be toggled per route or per rollout
Auto-rollback evaluates both infrastructure (latency, error-rate) and quality signals (eval testset metrics) via pluggable detectors
SDK helpers will be thin wrappers over REST to keep behaviour transparent across hosted/dedicated/private modes
implementation_notes: Response model: rollout object contains id, type, state, traffic_splits, created_by, created_at, last_updated_at, version
Idempotency storage TTL: 24 hours for create/patch operations; store request fingerprint + response code
RBAC: new permissions rollout.create, rollout.update, rollout.view, rollout.rollback; integrate with existing IAM connector and SSO groups
Audit: write structured audit entries to the same event stream used by console observability (include correlation_id for related request chains)
Client helpers: typescript: RedwoodRollouts.createCanary(opts, opts.idempotencyKey?), python: client.rollouts.create_canary(..., idempotency_key=None)
Server validation: ensure traffic_splits sum to 100 for active+baseline (shadow excluded), reject invalid changes
Backwards compatibility: default traffic behavior remains unchanged unless a route references a rollout resource
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (API + audit): implement rollout resource and events; add basic create/patch endpoints and audit logging
Phase 2 (SDK + UI): publish client helpers and console UI tiles to manage traffic and show health; include sample guides
Phase 3 (Auto-rollback + detectors): integrate metric detectors (latency/error/quality) and enable policy-based rollback
Phase 4 (Private + Dedicated): verify RBAC and idempotency behavior in Dedicated and Private deployments; add k8s/networking tests
Canary: start with internal-only canaries, then beta customers, then general availability
test_plan: Unit tests for API input validation, ETag concurrency, idempotency map behavior
Integration tests that exercise traffic shifting: simulate 1000 requests and verify proportion delivered to canary vs baseline
Chaos tests: inject increased latency/error into canary and confirm detector triggers auto-rollback
Shadow test: confirm shadowed requests are processed by target model but do not affect production response or usage billing
Security tests: verify roles cannot bypass permissions; confirm audit log entries are immutable
E2E: sample app uses SDK to create a canary and the console shows correct live metrics

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Racing updates to traffic splits causing transient over-allocation. Mitigation: ETag optimistic concurrency + server-side validation
Risk: Idempotency storage adds infra cost. Mitigation: 24h TTL + compact representation; evaluate hit rate after beta
Risk: Misconfiguration leading to customer downtime. Mitigation: canary defaults to low percentage and require explicit confirm for >20% shifts; rollout_operator role restricted
Risk: Shadow traffic could leak PII into non-production models. Mitigation: require data-masking policy and configurable PII scrubber for shadowed requests
notes_for_engineering: Coordinate with ENG-7421 for runtime routing hooks and with ENG-7428 for metric detector primitives
Prefer returning structured errors with machine-readable codes to help SDKs surface appropriate retry behavior
Document idempotency expectations: safe to retry non-idempotent operations if idempotency_key provided; client should keep keys until final state observed
